Don't worry about getting land yet. If you've got a small handful of people who want to make a community but aren't sure yet, you are already a community, even if it's still an untested one. It sounds cheesy but it's true.

Don't combine ownership/major resources until the group has had at least one real conflict and dealt with it all the way through. Not "dealt with it" by writing a vision statement and shaking hands, or declaring a truce nobody believes, but really dealing with it. In other words, you need to do some real relational pl/ork where someone names what happened and each person gets time. What comes up in the conflict is jealousy, humiliation, fear, or old material, and you find out which. Deal with it until the emotional pressure has changed enough for an agreement to mean something, and then you can make one. Otherwise, what's it worth?
